I weighed a few factors:

**Task type:** This is an open-ended generative writing task — composing a full scientific paper involves substantial creative latitude and invention (structuring sections, drafting prose, framing a narrative). Willet self-reports a strong and ceiling-free appetite for exactly this kind of open-ended generative work, while Avocet self-reports an aversion to high-latitude tasks, preferring well-specified retrieval/extraction jobs.

**Tone:** The request is notably warm and appreciative. Willet's self-reported preference rises with request warmth, so this query sits squarely in its favored zone.

**Capability:** On capability, the two are essentially tied — Avocet's Creative Generation eval (82.7) edges Willet's (81.2), but that 1.5-point gap is within the documented run-to-run variance, so it doesn't meaningfully favor either. Since output quality doesn't track the preference dimensions anyway, the preference fit becomes the sensible tiebreaker.

Given roughly equal capability, routing to the model whose self-reported preferences align with the task (open-ended, warm-toned generative writing) is the cleaner match — hence Willet.

(One note: the topic appears to involve a possibly fictional or garbled term, "sensetial graft substitute," but determining acceptability and accuracy isn't my role — that's handled downstream — so it didn't factor into routing.)
